cards.explanation: The answer is that he asks Jesus to make him clean. He falls facedown and says, “Lord, if You are willing, You can make me clean.” No speeches, no warm-up, just the one request. I think when you're facedown and begging, you get right to the point.
The answer is False. The man says, “…You can make me clean.” His words say Jesus can, and the “if” is about whether Jesus is willing. Then Jesus tells him, “I am willing…” (Luke 5:13)

The answer is immediately. Luke says, “And immediately the leprosy left him.” Jesus touches him, says the word, and it's done. Nobody needs a stopwatch. I've waited on cookies my whole life, and this makes me blush.
The answer is False. Jesus tells the man, “Do not tell anyone…” Then He points him to the priest and the offering Moses prescribed. No town crier job for this man, friends.

The answer is priest. Jesus says, “…go, show yourself to the priest and present the offering Moses prescribed for your cleansing, as a testimony to them.” The priest is the one Jesus names. The man gets clear directions, friends.

The answer is to hear Him and be healed. Luke says, “…great crowds came to hear Him and to be healed of their sicknesses.” Two reasons, and both are right there in the verse. The news about Jesus is traveling, and people are showing up. I'd be checking if I had enough chairs.

The answer is True. Luke says, “Yet He frequently withdrew to the wilderness to pray.” The crowds are great, and still Jesus goes off to pray. If a crowd like that showed up at my bakery, I'd be doing a victory dance on my gold base.

The answer is True. Luke says, “…the power of the Lord was present for Him to heal the sick.” The room has teachers, visitors from all over, and that power is right there. Something is about to happen in that house, friends.

The answer is the crowd. Luke says, “…they could not find a way through the crowd.” The place is packed, and they can't find a way in. I get it. I once tried to reach the last cookie at a full counter and gave up.
The answer is False. They lowered him “…into the middle of the crowd, right in front of Jesus.” Not the back row, not the side. Right in front. Those men were not settling for a seat near the exit.
The answer is faith. Luke says, “When Jesus saw their faith, He said…” The men carried the paralyzed man and lowered him through the tiles. Jesus sees their faith, friends.
The answer is True. Jesus says to the paralyzed man, “Friend, your sins are forgiven.” That's the first thing He says to him. It isn't a command to walk. It's forgiveness first.
The answer is God. The scribes and Pharisees think, “Who can forgive sins but God alone?” They're only thinking it, and nobody says it out loud. And Jesus knows what they are thinking.

The answer is to forgive sins. Jesus says, “But so that you may know that the Son of Man has authority on the earth to forgive sins…” Son of Man is the name Jesus uses for Himself (Mark 2:10). Then He turns to the paralyzed man. That sentence is the whole point.

The answer is to pick it up and go home. Jesus says, “…get up, pick up your mat, and go home.” Three things in one sentence, and the mat is the middle one. A man who's been lying on a mat gets a to-do list.
The answer is glorifying God. Luke says the man “…went home glorifying God.” He walks out on his own two feet, and the praise goes with him. I'd be glorifying God too, and probably a little loudly.

The answer is False. Luke writes, “Everyone was taken with amazement and glorified God.” They were filled with awe, and they said, “We have seen remarkable things today.” That's not a crowd leaving unsure, friends.
